items.title: Matthew Maxey Interview, 1960-01-12
items.q: The name 'Alberta' is mentioned by the interviewer addressing the interviewee, but the interviewee does not mention Alberta in their response, nor does the text describe any personal interaction or relationship between Matthew Maxey and Alberta.

ctx.x: I suppose you're singing Take This Hammer. That's one of the ones that you sing, I see, on the record. Uh, Alberta, I'll let you bang and grow long. What would you be singing about as you go along? You might sing about Take This Hammer. You're singing about the work you do. Now, Alberta, you're singing about women. What else might you sing?

Well, I mean, you be singing about women at the same time, but that's the same time you're singing to your hammer. You're singing to the tools that you are really working with. Singing to them. That's right. What's never that you be doing while you more than have to be singing to it? Well, it don't make no difference. You could be using the shell. You're going to catch a type of music that would follow your type of work. So, that looks like makes a man day go by easy, where he can be singing all along and working…
